protocol.runner_note: The measured /tmp wrapper and retained scripts/qwen35_gguf_redline_bench.py are byte-identical. The wrapper configures require_pm4=True, then removes LD_PRELOAD from the child environment while retaining the already-mapped interposer in Python. Substitute the retained path to reproduce from the committed tree.

transport_proof.strict_proof: is_pm4 at instantiate and before/after every launch

performance.interpretation: Retained PM4 improves the repeated-token graph decode and both capture-inclusive and steady post-load walls. Capture itself is slower and prefill is within the 0.5% guard. Two processes per transport are sufficient for this narrow diagnostic, not a broad package-default claim.

persistent_soak.initial_mechanical_failure: The benchmark forgot to reset Qwen35GGUFDecodeGraph.replayed_steps before reuse; run 2 stopped before launch. Commit 24b23b1e6 resets only that host counter alongside the existing device-position reset, after which the declared four-run gate passes.

known_blockers: The separate one-process 240-row same-HSACO matrix still faults at address zero after 48 rows; family isolation is not a production fix.
Redline upstream can execute one native shadow launch before strict post-launch proof detects a replay-time PM4 fallback.
No 4K-context, natural-prompt/category, concurrency, cancellation, or server lifecycle gate has run.
The Python-enabled interposer must be removed from LD_PRELOAD in the child environment so non-Python subprocesses are not injected with unresolved Python symbols.
Upstream build.rs requires mold even when mold is unavailable; the local build used an explicit temporary linker wrapper without source modification.
